questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of semiconductor RAM. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Advantages of Semiconductor RAM:
  • High Speed: Access times are very fast, often measured in nanoseconds.
  • Efficient Performance: Ideal for CPU cache (SRAM) and main memory (DRAM)
  • due to low latency.
  • Compact & Lightweight: Small size makes them ideal for smartphones, laptops,
  • and tablets.
  • Low Power Consumption: Generally consume less power compared to other
  • storage types.
  • Reliability: No moving parts mean they are more durable and shockproof.
  • Disadvantages of Semiconductor RAM:
  • Volatility: Data is lost when the power is turned off.
  • High Cost: Typically more expensive per gigabyte compared to non-
  • semiconductor storage technologies.
  • Lower Capacity: While improving, they have lower storage densities compared to
  • Hard Disk Drives (HDDs).
  • Limited Lifespan (DRAM): Requires constant power and periodic refresh cycles
  • (for DRAM) to maintain data.
  • Sensitivity: Semiconductor chips are sensitive to environmental factors like high
  • temperature and radiation.

questions.question: Define a parity generator. Explain the working of an even and odd parity generator with suitable examples. / [CO3] [5x4 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Definition – 2 marks. Explanation -3 marks.
  • There are two primary types of parity generators:
  • Even Parity Generator: It produces a parity bit such that the total number of 1s in
  • the code word is even.
  • If the data has an odd number of 1s, the generator sets the parity bit to 1.
  • If the data has an even number of 1s, the generator sets the parity bit to 0.
  • Odd Parity Generator: It produces a parity bit such that the total number of 1s in
  • the code word is odd.
  • If the data has an even number of 1s, the generator sets the parity bit to 1.
  • If the data has an odd number of 1s, the generator sets the parity bit to 0.
